paragraphs: Menachem, head of the court under Hillel.

In Chagigah ch. 2, mishnah 2, they said: Hillel and Menachem did not disagree (on the matter of semikhah [laying on of hands] on a festival); Menachem went out, Shammai entered (in his place). And they said in the Gemara there, 16b: Where did he go out to? Abaye said: He went out to tarbut ra'ah [evil ways]. Rava said: He went out to the king's service. It was taught likewise: Menachem went out to the king's service, and eighty pairs of students went out with him.
Antiquities relates that Menachem was a great sage who predicted in Herod’s youth that Herod would rule Israel.

Hyman suggests that it is possible that Abaye and Rava did not disagree at all; but, as is known, Herod killed several of the sages of Israel, and therefore anyone who inclined after him they called one who 'went out to tarbut ra'ah' [evil ways]. And he is not mentioned among the receivers of the Torah in Avot.

notes.text: Hyman proposes that the two explanations of Menachem’s departure may coincide; this is not adopted as an independently verified account of Herod’s court. The youth clause concerns the prediction about Herod.

The consulted Chagigah 16b directly records the eighty pairs and the different explanations by Abaye and Rava. The exact Antiquities passage and Hyman’s proposed historical reconciliation have not been independently verified here.
